quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, where should you position your vehicle?

options.text: Position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
Move closest to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so other drivers can see you as early as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the part of your lane where other drivers can see you first.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press the handgrip on the side where you want to escape. Use a small amount of pressure.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they actually are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle like a motorcycle really is. Do not assume other drivers can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave in your lane.
Maintain eye contact with other road users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the best way for other drivers to see your motorcycle. Check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: What type of shoes are best for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Sneakers
Leather boots
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the most protection when riding. They should be high and sturdy to protect and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of unobstructed pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: A plastic face shield can protect you from:

options.text: Noise.
Dust.
Glare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face during a crash. It also protects against rocks thrown from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you remember?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the truck driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield stops your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riders going too fast for the weather.
Riders turning too wide in curves or turns.
Riders leaving the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders turning too wide in curves or turns.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-motorcycle crashes is riders taking turns too wide. Turning too wide can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on (and your running lights if you have them). Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Where is there the most danger of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: The greatest danger of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles happens at intersections.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Do not position yourself so your arms have to hold up your body weight.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: They have definitely seen you.
It does not always mean they have really seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have really seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver has seen you. A driver can look directly at a motorcycle and still fail to notice it.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When it is raining.
When there is light traffic.
When it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if it takes longer to stop, you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy and vehicles might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is weaving on bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on bridge gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Do not zigzag to stay in your lane, as this is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagon signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane is safest when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases the risk of a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to pull back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What should eye protection do?

options.text: It is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
It is only needed in bad weather.
It should let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: Eye and face protection is required by law in California. A face shield protects your whole face if you crash. Good eye or face protection must let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: How should you sit to control a motorcycle properly?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns. Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to support your body. This position lets you easily reach all controls.

questions.question: How should a parked motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: How should a passenger hold onto the rider?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Do not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. Your passenger can also use secure handholds if available.
